snippet.title: Insanity (DOS) Complete Playthrough with all Wizard's Riddles
snippet.description:
Hello everyone!  This is LoZCardsfan2223 with another DOS game that brings me back to my early childhood and beyond.  It's also my first full playthrough on my channel!

Insanity was a game released in 1990 and is the sequel to Amaze. I played this a lot when I was a kid, but it wasn't a game that you could say I played religiously.  It was a nice change of pace game that I'd play a few times in a row then put away for a while before getting back into it.  

I have had this game for more than two decades, but I had never beaten it in my life.  In fact, I hadn't touched this game for at least the last dozen years!  Last night, I decided to give this game another shot and somehow, someway, I managed to beat the game on just my third try, but I didn't get it recorded because I did not expect to beat the game this quickly.  This video represents my second victory of the Insanity maze.

Here's how Insanity works.  You are in a gigantic maze and you have to find your way out by completing various challenges which when successfully completed will enable you to venture further into the maze.  

There are seven challenges in the game.  First is the Chocolate Fiend, then the Verbal Challenge (Words are Meaningless), then getting a man and woman into a church, then the Big Match (a soccer game you manage), then the Wizard's Castle (the hardest challenge in the game which will stop runs cold), then the Numbers Nightmare, and lastly the final challenge at the River to freedom.

However, just like Amaze, there are red fiends scattered in the maze that will search you out and kill you upon contact, but they are found much more sparsely.  I think there's only about a dozen red fiends total in the entire game (most of them in the final section).  Just like in Amaze, they can be shot with ammunition, but also just like in Amaze, they respawn when shot, sometimes almost instantly!

In Amaze, you started with three lives, but in Insanity, you only start with one life which means an early mistake, and your game is over!  However, you can collect additional lives by picking up double eighth notes.  Also scattered around the maze are the same "section" symbols from Amaze that will take away a life if you touch it.  You can also find extra ammunition which you will need to kill those pesky red fiends.  But you can only carry 10 items at a time.  That's right, I said items because you can pick up more than just bullets.  You'll see what I mean when you watch the video.

There are also new items in Insanity.  There's a question mark which gives you a riddle from the Wizard.  The more riddles you collect, the more helpful they become which can help you solve certain parts of the game.  Also, you'll find single eighth notes, which represents a random item and can be a gamble.  They can give you extra lives, riddles from the Wizard, and even an anti-gravity machine, which will let you see what the entire maze looks like rapidly.  However, a single eighth note can also cost you a life, particularly if you have a lot of extra lives in reserves.  If you have no extra lives in reserves, then a single eighth note almost certainly will give you an extra life.

Also, to make things even more insane, you are only given 30 minutes to complete the entire game!  That means you can't dilly-dally trying to find your way out.

You score points by navigating your way through different parts of the maze, but at a much slower rate.  You earn 50 points for shooting a red fiend and the following bonus points for completing these tasks:

Solving the Chocolate Fiend: 300 points
Finding the Hidden Lever: 100 points
Cracking the Verbal Challenge: 500 points
Getting the Couple to the Church: 200 points
Winning the Big Match: 300 points
Solving the Wizard's Challenge: 500 points
Getting Through the Numbers Nightmare: 100 points
Completing the Game: 2,500 points

Unlike Amaze, Insanity does have a high score table which you'll see at the end of the run.

Overall, this was a very solid run of Insanity with very few mistakes.  As far as I know, this is a FOYT (First on YouTube).  I know that some people who were diehard MS-DOS gamers and fans of Insanity had wanted to see a complete playthrough of this game for years, and I hope this presentation of Insanity got the job done!

Yet again, I apologize for the mouse cursor embedded into the video, I forgot to take it away on the OBS setup when recording.  Whoops!

This video is for entertainment purposes only.  No challenge to ownership is implied.  Insanity belongs to the respective copyright holders.
